title: Client predictive sampling: reduce hotpath tracing cost by estimating tail probability
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: several services report ~15-30% CPU and allocation overhead from full-span tracing on the hotpath, primarily due to span encoding and metadata enrichment for low-probability tail requests. Existing approaches (uniform probabilistic sampling and heavy-prefiltering) either miss tail events or still pay material hotpath costs for metadata collection.

Proposal: implement a small client-side predictive sampler embedded in the ingress/client agent that computes a fast 'tail probability' score and uses it to decide whether to emit a full span, emit a compact digest, or defer full-span reconstruction. The model is intentionally tiny (a calibrated logistic model / small decision tree compiled as arithmetic operations) so inference is lock-free and branch-friendly on the hotpath.

Key design points:
- Features: route_id, requested_max_tokens, KV-cache-hit-flag, recent route p50/p95 latency (local rolling window), tenant SLO slack (derived from route config), upstream-error-flag. All features are integer/enum-friendly so runtime cost is minimal.
- Decision modes: FULL (emit full span), DIGEST (emit compact token with provenance + minimal headers), DEFER (emit lightweight trace hint for async post-hoc expansion).
- SLO-aware thresholds: per-route thresholds controlled by config (console/rollout policies) so customers with strict latency SLOs keep minimal overhead while still retaining tail retention for debugging.
- Fallbacks: if the model or config fails, fall back to current default sampling policy.
- Offline training & telemetry: nightly retraining pipeline that updates the lightweight coefficients and pushes signed models to agents; training uses labeled tail events from our replay/incident corpus.

Targets / success metrics:
- Reduce median per-request tracing allocations on hotpath by >=40% for sampled traffic in canary tenants.
- Reduce p99 tracing-induced CPU time on critical ingress service by >=25%.
- Maintain tail-event retention accuracy (probability of full-span for true-tail events) >=85%.
- No increase in application-level p99 latency outside +/-0.5ms during canary.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Feature plumbing (2 weeks): add low-cost feature hooks in ingress proxy and client SDK; expose per-route SLO values to agent.
2) Model infra (1 week): implement lightweight model loader, signature verification, and inference routine in Rust shared-lib.
3) Decision logic + emit modes (2 weeks): wire decision -> emission paths (FULL/DIGEST/DEFER), implement compact digest schema.
4) Telemetry and eval (1 week): add metrics for model confidence, true-positive tail detection, digest reconstruction hits, and tracing bytes/sec.
5) Canary rollout (2 weeks): 5% tenants -> 20% -> 50% with rollback gates.

Trade-offs considered:
- Doing scoring server-side would give more context but adds network hop and latency. We prefer client scoring to avoid hotpath RPCs and to act early for allocation savings.
- Model complexity: we avoid complex neural nets to keep binary size and inference cost tiny; accuracy trade-off is acceptable because we can tune thresholds per-route.
- Digest format: adding a digest increases post-hoc reconstruction complexity; we mitigate by retaining provenance tokens that allow reconstructing full spans offline when needed.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/OBS/Client+Predictive+Sampler+Design
- Training notebook & dataset: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleTailDataset
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-observability/pull/4211
- Grafana dashboard for canary metrics: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/trace-sampler/ingress-predictive-sampler
- Incident postmortem used as seed labels: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PM/INC-2025-09-17-Ingress-Slowdown

Rollout safety and observability:
- Canary gates measure: change in tracing bytes/sec, allocations/request, CPU % on ingress, p99 app latency, and tail retention accuracy. All gates are automated in the release pipeline.
- Emergency rollback: agent config supports 'disable-predictor' flag via remote config; will be used if p99 app latency regresses >0.8ms or tail retention accuracy drops <75%.

Open questions / risks:
- Noise in local rolling latency windows leading to false positives; mitigated by smoothing + minimum sample counts before model can act.
- Model update drift: need guardrails so a bad model push can't increase full-span emissions; use signed models + staged rollout.
- Cross-tenant variability: initial canary will use a mix of tenants to validate calibration.

Deliverables:
- RFC + design doc (Confluence) with feature list and schema for DIGEST (done).
- Rust inference lib and agent hooks (PR in review).
- Retraining notebook and evaluation harness (in progress).
- Dashboard and alert rules for rollout (in progress).
